own_scenes.desc: La segunda fuente del heavy, que se suma a la estructura del blues rock: letras misteriosas de viaje de ácido, ropa de colores y espectáculos de luces (el heavy conservará los light shows de 1967). Musicalmente es como el jazz pero con repetición de frases simples; no apunta a las piernas sino a la cabeza, y perderse en la música es «entenderla», un uso extático que el heavy retoma en clave dionisíaca. Muchos pioneros del heavy empezaron aquí: Judas Priest con Rocka Rolla, Lemmy en Hawkwind, Ted Nugent en los Amboy Dukes, Uriah Heep a caballo entre ambos, y Pink Floyd, cuyos discos conceptuales de finales de los setenta se acercan al heavy.

refs.q: Heavy metal added psychedelic/acid-rock music to the basic structure of blues rock.
refs.para: Heavy metal added psychedelic/acid-rock music to the basic structure of blues rock.¹² Hendrix was already on to much of the psychedelic style, including its focus on visuals. He died before heavy metal became a well-defined genre, but he exerted an enormous influence on the eventual emergence of heavy metal through his personal charisma and talent, and through his embodiment of the two major traditions that formed the foundation for the genre. Psychedelic music was noted for its mysterious, drug-trip lyrics, and for the colorful clothes and lighting that marked its performances. Musically, it is jazzlike, but with a distinctive repetition of simple phrases. Using few and simple chords, it creates a very complex whole. Like nineteenth-century romantic tone poems, such as Smetana’s “The Moldau,” which aim at re-creating an object musically, acid rock tries to re-create an LSD experience. Acid rock was aimed not at one’s legs or crotch, but at one’s head. It wasn’t dance music. Getting lost in the music was “getting” the music. This ecstatic use of music was taken up by heavy metal in a Diony-sian key, for heavy metal revels in the powers of life.
refs.chapter: Cap. 2: Heavy metal: la bestia que se niega a morir

refs.q: A final example of the linkage between acid and metal is the group Pink Floyd.
refs.para: A final example of the linkage between acid and metal is the group Pink Floyd. Formed inthe mid-1960s, Floyd was a major originator of acid-rock music and was as well known for its light shows as for its acid-inspired, trip-evoking lyrics. They transformed themselves into an art-rock band with the megahit Dark Side of the Moon, released in 1973. Their concept albums of the latter part of the decade, Animals and The Wall, are musically closer to heavy metal.

own_scenes.desc: En 1965 San Francisco se convierte en la ciudad más efervescente del país: los Grateful Dead tocan en los «acid tests» de Ken Kesey, nace la escena hippy y en 1966-67 llega el verano del amor. El acid-rock, evolución del folk-rock pensada como banda sonora del viaje de LSD, es el equivalente rockero de la pintura abstracta, el free jazz y la poesía beat: su gran invento es la «jam», con la guitarra eléctrica al mando y un espíritu zen en lugar del dolor del blues. Jefferson Airplane encarnan la era; los Grateful Dead inventan la improvisación colectiva libre (Anthem Of The Sun, Live Dead); Kaleidoscope, Moby Grape, Quicksilver, Blue Cheer o Fifty Foot Hose amplían el abanico. Monterey y Sgt Pepper (1967) convierten lo alternativo en mainstream. Fuera de California, Jimi Hendrix declara la guerra a la armonía occidental con su guitarra.

podcast.title: Decline in Popularity (Early 1970s)
podcast.body: In the early 1970s, many music fans abandoned the "mind-blowing acid rock" of the 1960s, opting instead for a softer, "Mellow" sound, reflecting a shift in musical tastes. "Many fans had deserted the mind-blowing acid rock and the hard-driving funk and the soulful R&B of the 60s and decided to go all soft."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Peak During 1960s Societal Upheaval
podcast.body: Acid rock, along with electric rock, reached its peak popularity during the "general upheaval of society in the 1960s." Its subsequent decline in the 1970s mirrored a broader societal mellowing. "The general upheaval of society in the 1960s has passed when acid rock and electric rock were peaking."
